The portfolio link (riyashah.design) and Behance are present, but no case-study content is directly reviewable here — so craft is inferred from process signals, not visual output. Pair-design critique exposure with a senior designer during internship
Capstone project shows awareness of real-world constraints (low-bandwidth, regional language)

dimensions.name: process_rigor
dimensions.evidence: You ran '8 unmoderated UserTesting.com sessions on a new onboarding flow; surfaced 4 unique blockers, 3 of which made it into the next sprint' — a concrete research-to-sprint pipeline. The design-debt audit (20 issues, 12 fixed) shows iteration discipline beyond just shipping.
gaps: No accessibility (WCAG) mention anywhere — no audit ownership, compliance checks, or accessible component notes
Design system contribution is maintenance-level (52 components maintained, doc written) — no authorship of token architecture or system design decisions
No moderated usability testing or synthesis methods (affinity mapping, journey mapping) described
strengths: Unmoderated usability testing with concrete sprint impact (3 of 4 blockers acted on)
Field research (in-person interviews, Ratnagiri) for a concept project shows self-directed rigor
Design-debt audit shows proactive process thinking beyond assigned scope
First internal design-system change doc — process documentation ownership

dimensions.name: business_alignment
dimensions.evidence: The progress report redesign produced a measurable lift: 'parent open-rate on the linked email from 28% to 41% in A/B test (n=4,200 households)' — a clear, statistically meaningful outcome with sample size cited. You describe being 'sole designer on the parent-app team,' implying cross-functional ownership. Research blockers feeding directly into sprint planning shows PM/eng integration.
gaps: No explicit mention of PM or eng partnership — no tradeoff negotiation or scope constraint described
No evidence of understanding technical feasibility constraints when making design decisions
Only one quantified outcome across all work; the 6 shipped features during internship have no metrics attached
strengths: A/B test result with real sample size (n=4,200) — rare and strong for entry level
Shipping mindset evidenced by converting research blockers into sprint items
Sole designer ownership of a product surface demonstrates end-to-end accountability

dimensions.name: communication
dimensions.evidence: You wrote the first internal 'how to file a design-system change' doc, showing written communication capability. gaps: No design rationale documentation described for any shipped feature
No evidence of cross-team alignment work (eng handoff process, redlines, annotation style)
No external communication signals (writing, speaking, open-source contribution)

strengths: Internal process documentation (design-system change doc) shows written clarity

Pair-design critique sessions show comfort with structured feedback loops

dimensions.name: trajectory
dimensions.evidence: You converted from intern to FT at the same company within 9 months, moved from shipping 'small-to-medium features' to owning a full product surface (parent app), and took on system maintenance and documentation — clear upward progression in a short window. Domain has stayed within EdTech/mobile, which is coherent but narrow.
gaps: Single employer, single domain — no evidence of adaptability across product types or industries
No tool depth growth described beyond Figma/Maze/UserTesting.com stack
No mentorship given — receiving mentorship only, appropriate for entry but trajectory ceiling is visible
strengths: Intern-to-FTE conversion is a strong early signal
Scope expansion from feature execution to product surface ownership within one year
Self-initiated side project (Daily-Tide) outside employer domain shows proactive growth

output.candid_summary: You have a meaningfully stronger entry-level profile than most: a real A/B test result with sample size, field research on a self-directed project, and a component library contribution are signals most entry candidates lack. The 28%-to-41% open-rate lift is the single most impressive line on your resume — make sure it leads every case study. The two most important gaps to close before your next job search are accessibility (WCAG is entirely absent from your profile, and any senior designer will ask about it in the first interview) and cross-functional partnership language — you owned a surface solo but never describe how you worked with PM or eng on tradeoffs, which will read as a blind spot at mid-level interviews you will face in 12–18 months.

next_steps.action: Complete a WCAG 2.1 accessibility audit on one of your existing shipped screens (progress report or onboarding flow) and add the findings and fixes to that case study on riyashah.design.
next_steps.why: Accessibility is absent from your entire profile. Any design team with a senior designer will screen for this at entry level, and the gap will cost you interviews.

next_steps.action: Rewrite two portfolio case studies using a strict Problem → Research → Decision → Outcome structure, explicitly naming what you told engineering vs. what you cut for scope and why.
next_steps.why: Cross-functional tradeoff language is missing. Case studies that show you made real scope or feasibility calls will distinguish you from candidates who only describe visual output.

next_steps.action: Add metrics or qualitative outcomes to the 6 features shipped during your internship — even session completion rate, error rate drop, or a quoted PM response counts if you have no A/B data.
next_steps.why: Only one of your seven shipped work items has a measurable outcome. Reviewers will notice the gap and discount the other six as unvalidated work.

next_steps.action: Take the Deque University 'Accessibility Fundamentals — Disabilities, Guidelines, and Laws' free course and add it to your resume under certifications.
next_steps.why: Pairs with the audit action above; gives you a credential to cite when accessibility comes up in screens before interviewers can review your portfolio.

next_steps.action: On the Daily-Tide project, expand the Figma prototype to cover at least one error state and one edge case (e.g., no tide data available), and document your decision in the case study.
next_steps.why: Prototyping depth is unstated in your profile. Showing edge-case thinking in a concept project is the fastest way to signal interaction design maturity without a new work assignment.

next_steps.action: Add one paragraph to each case study describing how you aligned with or handed off to an engineer — even a brief Slack thread summary, annotation system, or sprint-planning moment counts.
next_steps.why: The 'sole designer' framing currently reads as working in isolation. Cross-functional partnership is a rubric dimension every design hiring manager evaluates.

next_steps.action: Write one 600–900 word article on your Daily-Tide field research process (what you learned interviewing fishermen, what surprised you) and publish it on Medium or your portfolio blog.
next_steps.why: External communication signals are absent. A single thoughtful piece establishes a voice and gives interviewers something to reference before your first call.

Riya Shah

With a year of full-time and internship experience as a product designer at an EdTech startup, I bring practical skills in owning feature designs and maintaining design systems, well-aligned with CRED’s need for a Junior Product Designer to contribute to the rewards-and-loyalty squad.

Best,
Riya
